Facts:
Beams Philippine Export Corporation filed a Petition for Review on Certiorari under Rule 45 of the Rules of Court.
The Petition assailed the Court of Appeals' Resolutions dated November 28, 2007 and May 28, 2009.
The Court of Appeals' Resolutions in CA-G.R. SP No. 03081 dismissed the petition for certiorari filed by Beams Philippine Export Corporation.
Marianita Castillo and Nida Quirante are the respondents in the case.
Issues:
Marianita Castillo and Nida Quirante were charged with 16 counts of Estafa.
The charges stemmed from conspiracy, confederation, and mutual assistance in issuing, encashing, and misappropriating the proceeds of the petitioner's checks.
The cases were raffled to the Regional Trial Court (RTC) of Cebu City, Branch 7.
The cases were docketed as Criminal Cases Nos. CBU-56537 to CBU-56552.
On August 30, 2007, the RTC dismissed the criminal cases for estafa.
The dismissal was based on the ground that the acts complained of do not constitute the crime of estafa.
A Motion for Reconsideration was filed on September 7, 2007.
The RTC denied the Motion for Reconsideration in an Order dated September 28, 2007.
The petitioner filed a petition for certiorari with the CA to assail the RTC Decision dated August 30, 2007, and Order dated September 28, 2007.
On November 28, 2007, the CA dismissed the petition.
The CA dismissed the petition because it was not filed by the Office of the Solicitor General (OSG).
The CA stated that the OSG must represent the People of the Philippines when criminal actions are brought to the CA or SC.
The CA also found defects on the Verification/Certification for Non-Forum Shopping of the Petition.
The CA cited violation of Section 1, Rule 65 of the Rules of Civil Procedure due to failure to attach relevant and pertinent pleadings and documents to the petition.
The petitioner filed a Motion for Reconsideration.
The CA denied the Motion for Reconsideration in a Resolution dated May 28, 2009.
The main issue is whether the CA erred when it dismissed the petition for certiorari under Rule 65 filed by the petitioner.
The dismissal was due to lack of authority to file the petition.
Rulings:
In Bautista v. Cimeta-Pangilinan, the Supreme Court ruled that only the OSG, representing the State, can appeal the acquittal or dismissal of a criminal case.
A private complainant may only question the acquittal or dismissal with respect to the accused's civil liability.
The petitioner's certiorari petition before the Court of Appeals sought reconsideration of the criminal aspect of the RTC decision.
The petitioner's "Discussion" in the petition for certiorari argued the evidence proved estafa, the RTC gravely abused its discretion in dismissing the case and ordering new Informations.
The petition lacked any claim for civil liability.
The petitioner only sought to appeal the dismissal of the criminal case.
The petitioner lacked the legal standing to question the RTC decision.
The petition is denied and the Court of Appeals' Resolutions dated November 28, 2007 and May 28, 2009 are affirmed.
